title: Global constructibility from affine-local constructibility
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring. Choose either the small étale site or the small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an immersion $i:Z\to X$, write $F|_Z=i^{-1}F$ with constant coefficients [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Say that this restriction is locally constant with finitely presented values if it has a covering on the chosen site of $Z$ on each member $V$ of which it is isomorphic to the constant module sheaf $\underline M_V$, for some finitely presented $R$-module $M$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. The module $M$ may vary with $V$ and need not be finite as a set.

The following conditions are equivalent: (i) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, there is a finite stratification $U=\coprod_a Z_a$ [def-constructible-stratification] by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-weil-constructible-subset], such that each $F|_{Z_a}$ is locally constant with finitely presented values; (ii) there is one finite stratification $X=\coprod_b S_b$ by constructible locally closed subschemes such that each $F|_{S_b}$ is locally constant with finitely presented values. The equivalence holds separately for either choice of site, with no finiteness assumption on the underlying set of $R$.

source.place: Tag 095E, lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated, Noetherian module version and finite-refinement proof. The same partition/refinement argument applies to pro-étale module sheaves (proetale.tex, definition-constructible); Noetherian-space constructibility is Tag 005L, topology-lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space.

proof.text: Choose the finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{a<n}W_a$ of the hypothesis. Each $W_a$ has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. By [lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian], their union $|X|$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]: every subset of $|X|$ is quasi-compact, including $X$ and every open subset. This also includes the empty scheme and the empty finite covering.

proof.text: The chosen affine cover makes $X$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], so [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes $X$ quasi-separated. Together with step 1, this verifies the qcqs hypothesis used below. In any open subspace $U\subseteq X$, every subset is quasi-compact: a cover in $U$ is a cover in the induced topology of that subset, to which step 1 applies. Consequently every open of $U$ is retrocompact. A locally closed subset $C\subseteq U$ has the form $O\cap(U\setminus V)$ with $O,V$ open in $U$; these opens are retrocompact, so $C$ is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. In particular this applies to every stratum of any finite stratification of an affine open.

We record the site operations used to restrict local models. For any scheme morphism $h:T\to Z$, base change sends an étale covering to an étale covering by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. The étale base-change functor preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] supplies its geometric inverse image and the inverse-image composition comparisons. For the pro-étale site all these assertions, including preservation of coverings and the comparison $(gh)^{-1}\cong h^{-1}g^{-1}$, are stated in [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. Hence for either fixed choice of site we may pull back a trivializing covering along $h$ and identify successive scheme restrictions with restriction along the composite. No coefficient finiteness is involved here.

proof.text:
For either site let $G$ on $Z$ have a trivializing covering $\{V_j\to Z\}$ with $G|_{V_j}\cong\underline{M_j}_{V_j}$ and $M_j$ finitely presented over $R$. Put $V'_j=T\times_ZV_j$. Step 3 gives a covering of $T$ and its restriction-composition comparisons. The scalar identifications and their compatibility with composition and localized restrictions are [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Applying [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] on $V'_j\to V_j$ gives module isomorphisms
$$ (h_R^*G)|_{V'_j}\cong (V'_j\to V_j)_R^*(G|_{V_j})\cong (V'_j\to V_j)_R^*\underline{M_j}_{V_j}\cong\underline{M_j}_{V'_j}. $$
The value is the same $R$-module $M_j$, so finite presentation is unchanged. Thus local constancy with finitely presented values is preserved by every scheme pullback. This is a direct application of the cited constant-module comparison to the pulled-back covering; it does not identify finite generation with finiteness as a set.

proof.text:
Assume (i). For each member $W_a$ of the finite affine cover in step 1 choose its supplied finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification $(Z_{a,b}\to W_a)_b$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core], whose statement is about schemes and has no restriction on sheaves or coefficients. Its qcqs hypothesis holds by steps 1 and 2. It gives a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification $(s_c:S_c\to X)_c$ and, for every $c$, indices $a,b$ and an actual scheme morphism $q_c:S_c\to Z_{a,b}$ such that $s_c$ equals the composite through $Z_{a,b}\to W_a\to X$. By the restriction-composition comparison of steps 3 and 4,
$$F|_{S_c}\cong q_c^*(F|_{Z_{a,b}}).$$
The right side is locally constant with the same finitely presented values by step 4 and (i). This proves (ii). The actual factorization supplied by the cited node is essential: mere containment of images would not suffice for arbitrary subscheme structures.

source.place: Tag 095E, lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated, proof (2) implies (3), using an immersed refinement with scheme factorizations

proof.text: Assume (ii), and fix any affine open $U\subseteq X$. Apply [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] to $U\to X$ and the given stratification $(S_b\to X)_b$. The actual base changes $T_b=U\times_XS_b\to U$ form a finite locally closed immersed stratification, with images the intersections of $U$ with the original stratum images. Step 2 makes every one of these locally closed subsets constructible in $U$. The projection $T_b\to S_b$ and the restriction-composition comparisons identify $F|_{T_b}$ with the pullback of $F|_{S_b}$. Step 4 therefore supplies local constancy with the same finitely presented $R$-module values on $T_b$. This proves (i) for every affine $U$, including the empty open. Both implications apply separately to the chosen site. In particular no part of the proof requires $R$ or its finitely presented modules to be finite as sets.
